description: Drawing Inferences is the process of extracting a logical deduction based on given facts and statements in Logical Reasoning. This information is not directly stated but is hidden within the context.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: To understand the process of drawing inferences, it is essential to know its core components.

key_concepts.explanation: The given information or fact that is considered 100% true to solve logical questions.
The logical outcome that can be definitively deduced from the given premise.
Information that is not explicitly written but is completely clear from the given context.

sections.title: Difference between Inference and Other Terms
sections.description: In exams, students often get confused between Inference, Assumption, and Conclusion.

results: An Assumption is what the author thinks before making the statement (Before the statement).
An Inference is what the reader deduces after reading the statement (After the statement).
A Conclusion is the final and main idea of the entire passage.
An Inference can be based on a specific part or a single fact within the passage.

sections.title: Identification of Correct Inference
sections.description: To identify a valid inference, certain specific parameters must be evaluated.

results: The inference must be 100% true and based only on the given passage.
It should not include any outside knowledge or personal opinions.
It might be true, but it cannot be 100% confirmed based on the given facts.
In competitive exams, this is generally considered false unless specifically asked.

sections.title: Steps to Solve
sections.description: A systematic approach should be adopted to accurately solve questions based on inferences.

steps.title: Analyze the Passage
steps.detail: Read the entire passage carefully to understand the core facts and the author's viewpoint.

steps.title: Evaluate Options
steps.detail: Read each option and check if it can be directly proven from the given facts in the passage.

steps.title: Eliminate Outside Information
steps.detail: Immediately eliminate options that are based on your general knowledge but are not mentioned in the passage.

steps.title: Identify Extreme Words
steps.detail: If an option contains extreme words like 'only', 'always', 'all', or 'never', it is generally a wrong inference.

sections.title: Common Mistakes and Rules
sections.description: To avoid negative marking in exams, students should avoid some common logical fallacies.

results: If the passage talks about a specific case or a few people, its rule cannot be applied to all.
If a statement says 'A causes B', it does not logically mean that 'B will always be caused by A' (Reverse logic is not always true).
